description: Type-scale and text utility classes for @exos/exos-theme-external. This theme ships a WIDER font-size scale than a standard exos theme: every size has BOTH a t-* and an equivalent fs-* alias, ranging from t-10/fs-10 (0.625rem) up to t-24/fs-24 (1.5rem) — note the extras t-10, t-20 and t-24 beyond the usual t-12..t-18. Headings h1–h4 are weight 700 and map onto the same scale. Also includes the `small-bolded-text` label utility (uppercase, weight 700, 10px) and a handful of literal semantic text/background color utilities defined in main.scss. Apply a size class to any text-bearing element; it is purely presentational.

always: Apply exactly one size class (t-* OR its fs-* alias) per element.
Prefer semantic heading tags (h1–h4) for document structure; reach for t-*/fs-* only for non-heading text or to override a heading's visual size.
never: Do not combine two size classes on the same element (e.g. `t-14 t-16`).
Do not invent intermediate sizes — only the literal t-10/12/14/16/18/20/24 (and fs-* aliases) exist.

a11y: Do not rely on font size alone to convey hierarchy; use proper heading levels for screen-reader structure.
Color utilities like text-white must keep sufficient contrast against their background.

size.description: Font-size step. Each value has an equivalent `fs-*` alias (e.g. t-16 == fs-16). Pick one.

t-10.note: 0.625rem. Alias: fs-10. Smallest caption / micro text.

t-14.note: 0.875rem. Alias: fs-14. Default body size in this theme.

t-20.note: 1.25rem. Alias: fs-20. Extra vs standard exos theme.

t-24.note: 1.5rem. Alias: fs-24. Largest step; extra vs standard exos theme.

alias.description: The fs-* aliases that mirror the t-* scale 1:1 (same font-size). Use either family interchangeably.

small-bolded.note: Uppercase, weight 700, 0.625rem, letter-spaced — used for small labels/eyebrows.

color.description: Literal semantic text-color utilities defined in main.scss (NOT a bootstrap generator — only these two exist literally).

white.note: color: white. For text on dark/gradient backgrounds.

tertiary.note: Tertiary text color. NOTE the source spelling is 'teritary' (typo preserved from the theme).
